checks.invariant: Dispatch-only baseline workflow: inputs cannot inject shell, the contents/pull-requests write token is used only to push a new branch and open a PR, and (as claimed at atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159) check_grants.mjs refuses to baseline grave indicators and exits 1 before writing.
checks.result: Inputs are `choice` and reach the shell only via env (no expression injection). Checkout keeps the default persist-credentials, so the write token sits in .git/config while dispatched-ref node scripts run (hardening). check_grants.mjs:158-170 writes every severity-'erro' finding to security_baseline.json and exits 0. It has no grave-type refusal, and git history shows none ever existed (candidate scripts/check_grants.mjs:--atualizar-baseline:grave-findings-baselined-without-refusal). DIVAT_ALVO is never read and the baselines have no per-target slots.

checks.invariant: Running the workflow's command `check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` against a live state with anon write grants, RLS off, a permissive write policy and a PUBLIC-executable function must fail closed and leave the baseline unchanged.
checks.result: With a fake psql and a dummy auditor URL in the sandbox, the normal gate first exits 1 and lists the grave findings. --atualizar-baseline then exits 0 and writes grant_escrita, policy_escrita, rls_off and funcao_public_execute into the baseline. The normal gate then exits 0 ('nenhum achado novo') against the same grave state.

checks.invariant: Ruleset updater: third-party registry content only reaches a new branch and a PR, the PR is merged by a human, no expression injection, and the write token is not handed to lower-trust inputs.
checks.result: Only workflow_dispatch triggers it. The ruleset list is fixed in job env. Downloads are checked for non-empty content and a `rules:` header and verified against the live registry. Only .semgrep/vendor/ is committed, to a new branch named per run and attempt, and every ${{ }} goes through env. Semgrep rules cannot execute code, so no lower-trust producer reaches the token. The persisted token is hardening only.

checks.invariant: The owner-only full-database credential (SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL, documented as never to be given to the agent) is bound to reviewed code, and only an age-encrypted package with sanitized logs leaves the job.
checks.result: Script-level controls hold. It requires a pooler URL with verify-full/system CA, opens a read-only snapshot, scrubs PG* env, prints fixed error categories only, uploads only the .age file (retention 30 days), unlinks the output on failure and does not persist credentials. However, the job declares no environment: and no ref guard. The secret is a repository secret per docs/backup.md:50, and the scripts/backup_private.py that receives it comes from whatever ref the dispatcher picks, while docs/backup.md:57 names the agent as the dispatcher (candidate github-workflows/backup-private.yml:SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL:repo-scoped-secret-unbound-to-ref).

checks.invariant: The scheduled public backup uses only the public anon key and exports only anon-readable public tables, so its 90-day artifact discloses nothing beyond the public API.
checks.result: Covered. The env carries only SUPABASE_URL and the public anon JWT. backup_rest.mjs:39-40 and :151 select PUBLICO mode, which excludes the four staging tables. The checkout does not persist credentials and the token is contents: read.

checks.invariant: Rendered trigger x secret x environment x checkout-credential matrix for the dispatch-only and backup workflows.
checks.result: No job declares `environment:`. backup-private passes SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY to the step running scripts/backup_private.py from the event ref. Both atualizar-* workflows check out with the default persisted credentials under contents/pull-requests write.

checks.invariant: Fork PR code never receives the auditor secret. PR-triggered jobs that hold a secret use a read-only token without persisted credentials, and no privileged trigger (pull_request_target/workflow_run/issue_comment) runs PR code.
checks.result: The fork-exclusion `if:` on every secret-bearing job is correct, and a null or deleted head repo also skips. No pull_request_target, workflow_run, artifact download or cache exists. Permissions are contents: read and persist-credentials is false. Same-repo PR heads do run PR-controlled scripts/check_*.mjs with SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL in job-level env. Because pull_request uses the PR's own workflow definition, a same-repo PR branch can also reference any repository secret, including SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL (path in candidate github-workflows/backup-private.yml:SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL:repo-scoped-secret-unbound-to-ref). The auditor credential alone is minimal (anon-inheriting diagnostics), so its own impact is low.

checks.invariant: Stated policy that the auditor secret is not exposed to PRs (phase3-security.yml:83-84, docs/seguranca.md:95).
checks.result: Holds only for phase3-security.yml (test-auditor runs on workflow_dispatch or push to main). The same secret is exposed to same-repo PR code by db-checks.yml:79-83 and deriva.yml:60-64, and phase3's workflow_dispatch accepts any ref. Docs and controls disagree. Folded into the secret-scope candidate as the low-impact variant.

checks.invariant: Secret-free PR jobs: no secrets, read-only token, no persisted credentials, no attacker-controlled ${{ }} inside run:, and no artifact reaching a privileged consumer.
checks.result: Covered. None references a secret. All use contents: read and persist-credentials: false. The only PR-derived expression (graft.yml concurrency group) is not shell. The graft artifact has no consumer.

checks.invariant: Rendered matrix of PR-reachable jobs: which secrets they hold, whether an environment gates them, and which repo scripts they execute.
checks.result: No job declares `environment:`. realtime, qualidade, seguranca and deriva expose SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL at job scope to every step, including the PR-controlled scripts/check_realtime.mjs, check_data_quality.mjs, check_grants.mjs, check_deriva.mjs and tests/check_grants.rig.mjs. ci, views, graft and semgrep hold no secrets.

candidates.title: Owner-only `postgres` backup credential is reachable from any agent-pushed or agent-dispatched ref (repository secret, no environment or ref binding)
candidates.description: docs/backup.md says only the owner registers SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and that the URI must never be sent to the agent, yet it names the agent as the one who dispatches the backup workflow. The credential is the `postgres` owner role of the sole production Supabase database (backup_private.py:45). It is set up as a repository secret, and backup-private.yml declares no `environment:` and no ref condition. Any identity that can push a branch and dispatch workflows (the AI agent sessions, which push branches and open PRs in this repo, or any other write collaborator or app) can therefore run backup-private.yml on its own branch. On that branch, scripts/backup_private.py, which receives the secret, is attacker-controlled. It can print the URI (for example base64-encoded to defeat masking), use it to write to the database, or encrypt the full dump to its own age key or none. The workflow then uploads that file as an artifact, which any signed-in user can download from a public repository. A second path needs no dispatch: same-repo pull_request runs (db-checks.yml, deriva.yml, which are required checks on every PR) execute the PR's own workflow definitions, so a PR branch that edits a workflow can reference any repository secret. Agent-authored commits in history (883640b, 9d9e594) modified workflow files, and the CHANGELOG records a temporary branch-pushed workflow that produced a database backup artifact. The auditor credential SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL is exposed the same way to same-repo PR code, contrary to phase3-security.yml:84 ('o secret não é exposto a PRs'), but its authority is minimal. The decisive facts are GitHub panel state: the secret's scope and the agent identity's permissions.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Secrets that grant authority above a branch writer are stored at repository scope and consumed by workflows whose code comes from a caller-selected ref (workflow_dispatch at any ref, same-repo pull_request). No GitHub Environment with a main-only deployment branch policy and owner approval binds them to reviewed code, so the documented boundary 'agent dispatches, but never receives the URI' is enforced by nothing.

trace.description: Manual dispatch with no input or ref restriction. Job `backup` (line 16) has no `environment:` and no `if:` on github.ref, so a dispatcher can run the workflow and scripts from any branch it pushed.

The script, as it exists on the caller's branch, reads the raw URI from the environment. All later handling, including the age recipient check at line 125, is code the caller controls.
The accepted credential is user `postgres.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk`, the database owner role with read/write authority over every schema, not a minimal read-only backup login.

Second path: same-repo PRs run the PR's own workflow files with repository secrets (fork PRs are skipped by the if: at line 79). A PR branch can add `${{ secrets.SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL }}` to any job. deriva.yml:47 behaves the same way.

evidence.description: Setup instructs 'Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret' for both backup secrets, so the scope is repository-wide, not environment.
Intended boundary: 'Só o dono cadastra; nunca enviar a URI ao agente/chat.'
'O agente dispara e acompanha o workflow.' The principal barred from the URI is the designated dispatcher.
Precedent: a backup was produced by 'um workflow temporário disparado por push na branch' (lines 1367-1369), so branch-pushed workflow code has received backup credentials in this repository.
Claims the auditor secret 'não é exposto a PRs', but db-checks.yml:83/101/131 and deriva.yml:64 hand the same secret to PR-head code: a lower-impact variant of the same scoping gap.
The only branch control is the main ruleset: PRs and checks, 'não exige aprovação humana'. Nothing restricts which refs secret-bearing workflows run from.

blockers: Not source-observable: whether SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY are currently configured, and whether they are repository/organization secrets or restricted to a GitHub Environment. The docs say repository secret, and backup-private.yml declares no environment, so an environment-only secret would not resolve.

Not source-observable: the GitHub identity and permissions the AI agent sessions (Claude Code / Codex) push and dispatch with (Contents write, Actions write for workflow_dispatch with an arbitrary ref, Workflows permission), and whether other write-level collaborators or apps exist.
Not source-observable: repository/organization Actions policies that could restrict which refs or actors may run workflows.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the GitHub web UI: (1) Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions: record whether SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY appear under Repository secrets (finding holds) or only under an Environment with deployment-branch and reviewer protection (finding does not hold). (2) Settings → GitHub Apps and Collaborators: record the Contents, Actions and Workflows permissions of the identity the agent sessions use. (3) Safe confirmation without the real secret: in a throwaway repository, create a repository secret DUMMY=marker, have the agent identity push a branch whose script prints only the secret's length, then dispatch the workflow on that branch. A printed length proves agent-chosen code receives repository secrets. Remediation to verify: move both backup secrets into an Environment (e.g. `backup-integral`) limited to `main` with the owner as required reviewer, and add `environment: backup-integral` to jobs.backup.
validation_plan.local: Regression after the fix: render the workflow trigger/secret/environment matrix (as in agents/h17-ci-secrets/artifacts/check-02.out). Require jobs.backup in backup-private.yml to declare the protected environment, and require that no job reachable from pull_request or from an unrestricted dispatch references SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL.

candidates.title: 'Atualizar baseline' promises grave security findings cannot be baselined, but check_grants.mjs writes anon write grants and RLS-off into the baseline and silences the daily gate
candidates.description: The dispatch-only workflow `Atualizar baseline` (contents/pull-requests write) is the documented mobile path to update scripts/security_baseline.json through a PR. Its header (atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21) states that, by design of the script, it cannot baseline one of the six grave indicators: check_grants.mjs refuses and exits 1 before writing. The PR body it generates (line 159) repeats this to the owner who decides the merge. The script has no such refusal: check_grants.mjs:158-170 writes every severity-'erro' finding, including grant_escrita (anon/authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE), rls_off, policy_escrita and funcao_public_execute, then exits 0. Once that PR is merged, the daily `seguranca` job (db-checks.yml:144), which ADR-0003 calls the control that protects the database, treats the live grave state as a known exception and passes. The realistic trigger is documented: supabase_admin default privileges grant anon write on new public tables and cannot be closed (db-checks.yml:13-17).
candidates.root_cause: The --atualizar-baseline branch of check_grants.mjs filters only on severity ('erro') and has no deny-list of non-baselinable finding types. The read side (lines 173-186) likewise accepts any baselined key, so neither the workflow nor a hand-edited baseline can be stopped from silencing grave findings. The workflow and PR text assert a control that git history shows never existed.
candidates.intended_behavior: `check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` must exit 1 without writing when any grave indicator is present (anon/authenticated write or MAINTAIN grants, RLS off, non-SELECT policies that do not block writes, PUBLIC-executable functions, permissive default privileges outside the documented supabase_admin limitation). The normal gate must never treat those types as known exceptions, as atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159 promise.

trace.description: A writer, or the agent acting for the phone-only owner, dispatches the baseline update to clear a red `seguranca` gate.
Runs `node scripts/check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` against the live database through the auditor credential.
Live anon write grants become `grant_escrita` findings with the default severity 'erro'. rls_off (line 111), policy_escrita (line 129) and funcao_public_execute (line 135) are built the same way.
The only filter is `a.severidade === 'erro'`. Every grave finding is serialized and written to scripts/security_baseline.json (line 167), and the process exits 0 (line 170).

trace.scope: steps['Abrir o PR com o diff'] gh pr create --body
trace.description: The PR body tells the merging owner 'Os seis indicadores graves não passam por aqui — o script recusa baseliná-los e sai 1 antes de escrever', which is false.
After merge, the baselined grave keys count as `conhecidos`, `novos` is empty and the gate exits 0 ('nenhum achado novo') while anon can still write.

evidence.description: Claimed control: 'baselinar um dos SEIS indicadores graves. `check_grants.mjs` recusa e sai 1 antes de escrever ... Este workflow não tem como contornar isso, e é de propósito.'
The --atualizar-baseline block writes all severity-'erro' findings with no type-based refusal. A git -G search across all refs finds no grave-indicator logic in scripts/ ever.
Daily cadence exists because supabase_admin default privileges grant anon write and cannot be closed, which is the expected source of a live grave finding.
'Sigilo não é o que protege o banco aqui; o gate diário é.' The silenced gate is the stated protective control.

conditions.description: A grave posture exists live in the sole Supabase database (e.g. a public table anon can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, as supabase_admin default privileges produce), so the daily seguranca gate is red.
A repository writer or workflow dispatcher (the owner, or the agent the docs designate to run Actions for the phone-only owner) runs 'Atualizar baseline' with baseline=seguranca.
The owner merges the generated PR, relying on its body's assertion that grave indicators cannot be included.

execution.attacker_perspective: A lower-trust state change (an anon-writable public table appearing live, for example via the unclosable supabase_admin default privileges) meets the documented 'Atualizar baseline' path. The workflow output, not a reviewer's own analysis, tells the owner the grave state could not have been baselined.
payloads: Fake psql response for the security shape: tabela_vista_teste anon {select,insert,update,delete,truncate}=true with a PERMISSIVE 'w' policy qual/with_check 'true'; evento_dados rls=false; divat_api_shape() public_execute=true, security_definer=true, search_path_fixo=false; postgres default privilege on public tables anon=INSERT
instructions: Copy scripts/check_grants.mjs, scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs, scripts/lib/security-policies.mjs and scripts/security_baseline.json into an empty scratch directory with the same scripts/ layout (same approach as tests/check_grants.rig.mjs).
Put a fake `psql` first on PATH that prints the grave security-shape fixture as one JSON line. Set the dummy auditor URL. Run with no network.
Run `node scripts/check_grants.mjs` and record the exit status. Run it again with `--atualizar-baseline`, then once more in normal mode against the same fixture.
Read the scripts/security_baseline.json the second run wrote.
execution.observed_result: Normal gate before: exit 1, '✗ POSTURA DE SEGURANÇA REGREDIU', listing [grant_escrita] anon tem INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE em tabela_vista_teste, [policy_escrita], [rls_off] RLS desligada em evento_dados and [funcao_public_execute]. --atualizar-baseline: exit 0, '✓ Baseline reescrito com 7 exceção(ões)'. The baseline now contains grant_escrita tabela_vista_teste:anon, policy_escrita tabela_vista_teste:anon_write_all, rls_off evento_dados and funcao_public_execute divat_api_shape(). Normal gate after: exit 0, '✓ Postura de segurança: nenhum achado novo', with the same grave state listed as known exceptions (agents/h17-ci-secrets/artifacts/check-01.out).

remediation.strategy: Implement the promised refusal in check_grants.mjs on both sides. On write, --atualizar-baseline exits 1 without writing when any grave type is present. On read, grave types in the baseline file are never honored, so a hand-edited baseline cannot silence them either. Keep the documented supabase_admin default-privilege and rls_auto_enable() exceptions baselinable. Add rig cases to tests/check_grants.rig.mjs: (a) --atualizar-baseline with anon INSERT → exit 1 and baseline byte-identical; (b) a baseline containing grant_escrita → gate still exits 1. Until then, correct atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159 so the PR does not assert a non-existent guard.

likelihood.reason: Requires a live grave posture, a deliberate dispatch of the baseline workflow and a human merge. The red gate and the documented phone-only path make that sequence plausible, and the PR text actively tells the reviewer the grave case is impossible.

impact.reason: An anon-writable or RLS-off table on the sole production database would stay live with the daily gate green. The gate is the stated protective control (ADR-0003), and the impact on data integrity is the anonymous writes it no longer reports.

confidence.reason: The source shows no refusal anywhere in history, and a sandboxed run of the real script copies with a dummy credential reproduced baseline write, exit 0 and a silenced gate.

hardening: atualizar-baseline.yml:73 and atualizar-semgrep-rulesets.yml:58 use actions/checkout with the default persist-credentials under contents: write + pull-requests: write. The token sits in .git/config while dispatched-ref node scripts (holding the auditor secret), apt, `pip install semgrep==1.171.0` with unpinned transitive dependencies, and registry downloads run. Only the final push needs it: set persist-credentials: false and pass GH_TOKEN only to the push/PR step.

Both updater workflows depend on the repository setting 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests'. With pull-requests: write, the same token could approve PRs. The main ruleset requires no approval today (docs/seguranca.md:73), so there is no current impact, but adding required approvals later would let any dispatcher self-approve through these workflows.

atualizar-baseline.yml:23-31 and :145 claim that `alvo: producao` fails closed and that only that target's 'slot' is written. check_grants.mjs and check_data_quality.mjs never read DIVAT_ALVO, and the baseline files have no per-target slots, so alvo=producao measures the SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL database and rewrites the single baseline. This is harmless with one database, but the commit and PR text are inaccurate.

db-checks.yml:82-83/100-101/130-131 and deriva.yml:63-64 set the auditor secret in job-level env, so every step (apt-get, tests/check_grants.rig.mjs) inherits it. Scope it to the single step that calls the auditor.

For fork PRs, the secret-bearing required checks (realtime, qualidade, seguranca, deriva) are skipped by the `if:`, and GitHub counts skipped jobs as passing required checks. Fork PRs therefore satisfy those four checks without any live audit (a writer still has to merge).
PRs opened with GITHUB_TOKEN by the two updater workflows do not trigger pull_request workflows, so the eight required checks never report on them until a human pushes or reopens.

backup_private.py:45 accepts only the `postgres` owner login. A dedicated read-only backup login (read-all-data, no write, no role administration) would shrink the blast radius of any exposure of SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL.

uncovered.boundary: repository-scoped VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET (job-level env) + host allowlist in scripts/check_deploy.mjs, script taken from the event/dispatched ref
uncovered.reason: The same repo-scoped-secret, ref-unbound root cause applies to the Vercel bypass secret, and the deployment_status/free-text-URL handoff is a separate boundary that no listed coverage unit owns.
